heroHeadline: China Completes Bilateral Tech War Architecture on June 2 — AI and Data Classified as Trade Secrets; 63-Sector Counter-Sanctions Blueprint Published
heroSubtitle: June 2, 2026 — One day after China and the US simultaneously enacted major bilateral technology control frameworks (June 1), Beijing completed a second layer of domestic IP protection: new 'Regulations on Trade Secret Protection' effective June 2 formally classify AI training data, model weights, and algorithms as legally protected trade secrets for the first time in Chinese law. The regulation provides civil and criminal enforcement tools against data exfiltration — operationalizing the June 1 outbound investment regime and May 26 talent travel restrictions into a domestic legal enforcement layer covering DeepSeek model architectures, Huawei Ascend chip designs, SMIC 7nm process technology, and CATL battery IP. Simultaneously, a Chinese government-affiliated research team published a comprehensive 63-sector framework identifying technology domains where China holds sufficient global market dominance to impose counter-sanctions on the US and allies — covering rare earth processing (~80% global share), solar panels (~90%), battery cells, drone components, and AI model architectures. The 63-sector framework mirrors the US Entity List architecture, creating a counter-sanctions deterrence capability blueprint that has never before been formally compiled. Together, the June 2 moves complete a four-layer technology protection architecture built in seven days: (June 1) outbound investment controls requiring approval for all overseas tech/data/personnel transfers; (June 1) US BIS global chip enforcement clarification extending jurisdiction to all Chinese-parented firms globally; (June 2) AI/data trade secret protection with domestic legal enforcement; (June 2) 63-sector counter-sanctions capability framework. China's tech ecosystem operational status as of June 2, 2026: DeepSeek V4 Pro at $0.003625/M input tokens (permanent); Huawei Ascend ~60% domestic AI chip market; BYD debuted in-house autonomous driving chip (May 28); China domestic AI accelerator market at 2.123M units/year (+136% YoY); combined valuation of China's AI unicorn wave at $135B+ — all funded by domestic capital structurally independent of US market access.
